claims.text: As-cast polycrystalline MnNiSi-based material has relatively coarse grains.
As-cast MnNiSi-based material has limited intrinsic toughness or mechanical robustness.
The magnetostructural transition in MnNiSi-based material produces a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
A tailored post-casting annealing treatment can induce nanometer-sized coherent precipitates within the MnNiSi matrix.
Fine coherent nanoprecipitates can form in grain interiors or at grain boundaries.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby provide precipitation strengthening.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates will increase the yield strength relative to the as-cast state.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates will improve ductility relative to the as-cast state.
The coherent and uniform distribution of nanoprecipitates will preserve the matrix-phase balance responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
The annealed material's peak magnetocaloric entropy change will remain within approximately 10% of the as-cast value.
The annealed material's transition temperature will remain within approximately 10% of the as-cast value.
Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates can substantially strengthen another magnetic alloy while retaining good ductility and causing only a marginal increase in coercivity.
Excessive annealing temperature or time can cause precipitate coarsening or an increased precipitate volume fraction.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or volume fraction can interfere with the magnetostructural transition and reduce magnetocaloric performance.
The proposed intervention is effective only within a narrow annealing-temperature and time window.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires entropy change and transition temperature to remain within approximately 10% of baseline in either direction, whereas the falsification rule only addresses reductions greater than 10%. An increase or upward shift greater than 10% would violate the prediction without clearly satisfying the stated falsification rule.
